original_question: Is there a birack whose induced action on virtual braids is faithful, and is the known invariant of virtual braids cited in [87] and [74, 3, 51] faithful?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s target almost verbatim: it asks both whether there exists a birack with faithful action on virtual braids and whether the virtual-braid invariant cited in [87], with cross-references [74], [3], and [51], is faithful. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states this specifically as Section 7, item 9, under the heading “Virtual braids,” so that location should be made explicit. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The second clause is not about an unspecified “known invariant,” but about “the invariant of virtual braids in [87], see also [74, 3, 51],” with [87] being Manturov’s paper “On the recognition of virtual braids.” ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, “faithful” should be spelled out as injective, i.e. distinguishing distinct virtual braids. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The nearby scope note says that the action defined by linear biquandles is not faithful, so the first clause should remain an unrestricted existence question over biracks and should not be narrowed to linear biquandles. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper does not fix a strand number n or single out one group VB_n; it leaves the problem at the general level of “virtual braids.” ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper’s wording is “its action on virtual braids,” not “induced action,” so the latter should be softened to stay maximally paper-faithful. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: Does there exist a birack whose associated action on virtual braids is faithful, and is Manturov’s invariant of virtual braids from [87]—also cited in [74], [3], and [51]—faithful, i.e. injective on virtual braids? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Problem 9 in Section 7 rather than any earlier theorem or conjecture: the wording on page 23 matches it almost exactly. Section 3.2 supplies the nearby algebraic context by defining biquandles and the switch/sideways-operator formalism behind braid-type actions, and Section 3.3.1 explains the virtual-biquandle extension at virtual crossings. The sentence immediately following Problem 9 states that linear biquandle actions are not faithful, so the refined question must preserve the paper’s unrestricted existential quantifier over biracks and must not narrow the problem to linear cases. There are no ambient ring, field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or “for sufficiently large m” conditions attached to this problem in the paper. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
